Immediate optimistic outcome; no server write before validation accepts.
Rejected action restores exact checkpoint and cancels dependent actions.
A new editor never reuses a prior value or confirmation flag.
Delayed close events cannot clear or close a newer editor.
Sync Off preserves microphone visibility and recognition.
One utterance cannot execute both a short command and its preempting continuation.
Returning from Trip Log preserves underlying editor value and surface.
Ready / End Trip uses one immutable timestamp for end/start boundary.
End <break type> OK skips question and dialog; standalone final End <break type> shows both.
Scheduled Start accepts a valid duration with or without the Standard Time prefix.
Break Selector is pointer-only; voice start commands use a typed OK/Cancel dialog.
Localized command patterns dispatch neutral interval identifiers; core logic does not parse English break names.
Only the End command matching the active semantic interval type is eligible.
Recognition off/sleep while voice editing switches to keypad and preserves value.
Trip summary stays until OK/Cancel; no automatic editor open.
A spoken range command announces Viewing once and suppresses mode feedback.
Selecting a range updates the current range, label and calculations immediately; a pending asynchronous settings save must not restore the previous range.
Every suppressed component identifies its rule and suppressing owner; optional is not the same as skippable.

Main standard_time_component is trip-only and its label is Standard Time in every scope. Header edit remains available during a normal active trip, including Down/Break/Lunch; standalone breaks have no standard. Aggregate accounting is unchanged.

Goal-bar Remaining = trip standard minus node counted position. Standard is 0:00 at 100%; Current is 0:00 at counted trip standard. Elapsed uses counted trip time, without prior aggregate elapsed history. End Time for every node, including Current, uses its trip counted position and the existing trip deadline formatter.
Idle nodes use configured goals. Active aggregate nodes use inferred current-trip requirements. Every goal editor edits configured non-inferred values; Standard edits time, not 100%.

Missed labels disappear and goals exit right; all failed retains Standard at right on a zero-to-100% scale with its time and percent details restored. Elapsed color occupies the right segment; all-failed Overtime runs from Current to final failed goal. Down uses its configured color; Break/Lunch colors do not replace productive bar colors.

Circles are opaque and packed using radius plus half each computed stroke width. Borders touch without overlap; miss pulses expand inward. Ticks travel with nodes. Labels have independent collision packing and leaders. Times/percentages share preferred 16px sizing.

Whole bar, including nodes, labels, background and compression triangles, opens the existing selector: Trip only in Trip mode, selected aggregate only in aggregate mode, both in Auto. Failure count does not filter choices. No Standard Time edit or Current time-mode action from the bar. Classic and Bar goal dialogs and pads show actual configured and inferred trip values; only actual is edited.

Above-150 user goal input becomes 150 before UI feedback. Correction sentence precedes recalculation and later chain announcements. Speech-passive notice never takes command ownership; audio batching does not serialize independent command slots.

Drop-In shares rendering and configured-goal selection. Observer permissions remain unchanged; publisher Standard Time is read-only. Raw configured publisher attributes take precedence over inferred UI goal components.

Existing node movement, failure exit, fitting and reduced motion are implemented. Load/start/end choreography is specified in goal-bar.md but remains proposed; do not infer deployed animation states from the specification.

Trip mode shows Standard, Trip and active Current; aggregate modes show Standard, selected aggregate and active Current; Auto shows both goal types. Idle follows the same goal visibility without Current. Hidden goals cannot enter failure markers or failed-goal choices. All active values are trip-based; aggregate goals are inferred trip requirements.
Active main Time Elapsed, Time Remaining and End Time readouts use the current trip and Trip labels in every percentage mode. Aggregate reporting remains unchanged.

Only the next target (highest unfailed visible goal) and Current show times and percentages. Other unfailed nodes retain circles, names and editing actions. All-failed retains Standard at the right with its time and 100% reference details, and Current on a zero-to-100% scale.

ui-persistence-behaviors.Wait Sync: Complete the operation before control returns; update UI only after acceptance.
ui-persistence-behaviors.Wait Async: Keep UI responsive and show pending status; update UI only after acceptance. Authentication uses Wait Async.
ui-persistence-behaviors.Optimistic: Asynchronous: update UI immediately while persistence is pending; restore the previous UI after rejection or failure.
ui-persistence-behaviors.Enforce: Asynchronous: update UI immediately; retain it while retrying a valid action until accepted. Cancellation or a command becoming invalid ends retries.
ui-persistence-behaviors.validation: All server writes require validation first, regardless of UI persistence behavior.
ui-persistence-behaviors.required: Every UI component that reads or writes persistence must explicitly declare persistenceBehavior: Wait Sync, Wait Async, Optimistic or Enforce for each operation. No implicit default. Shared pointer and voice paths use the same declaration.
ui-persistence-behaviors.testContract: Specify initial state, pending UI, accepted UI, rejected/failed UI, cancellation, stale completion after account or target switch, and retry behavior. Wait Sync must finish before control returns; Wait Async must remain responsive. Persistence reads declare the appropriate Wait variant and may retain a valid existing display while loading.
ui-persistence-behaviors.scope: These terms describe UI persistence policy, independently of command source, feedback and pending-operation status.

contracts.UI: Apply optimistic outcome immediately. Commands that are client-only do not access remote persistence.
contracts.server: For commands requiring persistence, validate before any write. Rejection restores the checkpoint and cancels dependent operations.
contracts.retry: Local transient storage failures retain optimistic UI and retry asynchronously with 150 ms exponential delay capped at 2000 ms. Abort ends retries. Remote-write retry/idempotency contract remains unresolved.
contracts.time: Durations and boundaries are milliseconds; absolute dates are timezone-aware. Finishing and confirming a new trip are separate user actions, not an automatic continuous boundary.
contracts.summary: Trip Summary can be requested at any time and speaks totals for every trip in selected range except current active trip. No data renders/speaks No trip data available. Both paths hold until OK/Cancel. trip-ended/system adds Say OK to start a new trip LAST; requested/voice or pointer suppresses that prompt and returns to prior focus on OK/Cancel. Range refresh preserves invocation. An automatic trip-ended summary immediately finishes a pending keypad close before taking focus; the old close timer cannot dismiss a newly opened editor.
contracts.voicepad: Voicepad access while disabled requests explicit recognition enable. OK enables recognition before opening; Cancel preserves current surface. Sleep/off while editing automatically preserves value and opens keypad.
contracts.settings: Settings focus coexists with trip/clock/range regions. Closing settings restores prior focus; persistence rejection restores state and dependent changes.
contracts.locale: Semantic state/range IDs remain stable. UI text, spoken command vocabulary, recognition patterns and announcement templates belong to the selected language pack.
contracts.aggregation: TripAggregates shared calculations: latest row wins per String(id); anonymous rows remain distinct. Range bounds inclusive from CalendarRange.tripWindow. Counted time uses persisted counted milliseconds, fallback actual; active trip counted=max(allotted,counted). percent=standard/counted (null at zero); banked=round(standard/goalPercent-counted). Summary includes both production/nonproduction, excludes running/current ID. Log keeps its production filter and existing active-trip inclusion rule. Results are immutable state.tripAggregates children, UI invocation stays state.tripSummary.
contracts.login: ID group OK advances to PIN. PIN group OK submits once, without a second OK or PIN readback. Failure retains ID and clears PIN. Raw PIN is never public state.
contracts.login-input: Keyboard/mobile Return and button OK share the voice confirmation path. Incomplete groups cannot submit. Repeated decoder partials cannot submit twice. Cancel and Backspace preserve their existing credential-entry rules.
contracts.startup: Request the localized loading announcement once during page initialization, without a startup dialog or OK gate. First ordinary pointer/keyboard gesture unlocks audio where required by browser policy. Login speech waits for startup onEnd/onError and recognition model readiness; UI initialization remains responsive. Only the current login prompt is released.
contracts.login-authentication: Authentication is not optimistic. Keep modal open and disable credential controls while a single request is pending. Only after acceptance may success be spoken or session/profile populated. Failure returns to first empty PIN with confirmed ID retained and a fresh PIN-group OK then final OK required.
contracts.profile-editor: Admin Edit Profile searches through account lookup; a single match selects and loads authoritative profile details automatically, multiple matches require selecting one. No match renders an error and clears the editor. Autogenerated account ID is readonly and excluded from writes; names, preferred name, username, replacement password, four-digit login ID, replacement PIN and permissions are editable subject to server authorization. Existing password/PIN are never returned or populated. Empty replacement secrets retain credentials; initial voice credentials require ID and PIN together, later independent edits preserve the other credential. Loading and saving disable editing; success is shown only after server confirmation. Rejected saves retain editable non-secret input and show the server error. Stale detail responses cannot populate a different selected account. Actor permissions are rechecked at the server.

Account Lookup hides profile editing controls. Both windows fit in the safe viewport above the mic bar and its expanded panes, recomputing on opening, resize, viewport scroll and mic boundary change; content scrolls inside the modal. Recognition off restores full viewport space. Edit Profile icon: person, magnifying glass lower left, pencil lower right.
contracts.trip-log-layout: Deleting/editing trips leaves focus on the open Trip Log; redraw and trip-state changes reconcile the open header/body/close controls against current viewport and mic safe boundary immediately and on the next frame. The closed button slot never determines open shell geometry. Removing the last trip shows settings/no-data inside the same open shell.

announcement-timing.ownership: AnnouncementCatalog owns speechStart.anchor and paddingMs; songs only provide notes, tempo, measured loudness and musical timing. No speech policy or spoken text in songs.
announcement-timing.calculation: AudioEngine.songTiming sums effect/sustain lengths, includes note offsets and rests, and takes maximum end across simultaneous notes. Effective BPM = song BPM Ã— selected chime rate. Playback reports remaining time from the audio clock including scheduling lead.
announcement-timing.normal: Speech is eligible after all notes and their selected-instrument release envelopes finish, plus announcement padding, then the existing speech-rate-scaled component margin (300 ms at 1Ã—). Between separate announcements, existing doubled margin remains.
announcement-timing.error: Down Time and Goal Failed speech is eligible at the start of the terminal sustain, with no extra end-of-chime margin. Error speech may overlap the sustained chord. Summary/details spacing remains unchanged.
announcement-timing.muted: No chime means no chime timing wait. Speech guards and queued cancellation still apply.
announcement-timing.volume: Measured RMS over musical duration and peak dBFS at reference volume are song metadata. Attenuation balances level and reserves peak headroom; user/master/per-announcement volume remains authoritative. No gain boost. Measurement is not LUFS and is not valid for a substituted instrument; phone/substituted instruments bypass unmatched calibration.
announcement-timing.note-delay: Tone events may specify finite non-negative noteDelayMs. Delay moves the actual note onset, musical end, sustain anchor and release end together; announcement readiness includes it. Delays do not shift speech directly or change tempo.

chime-easter-egg.status: Local audio mix; no speech trigger assigned
chime-easter-egg.beat: Steady unchanged-inspired pulse: one note every beat, identical note length, and equal gaps between every successive pulse note. May vary pitch in C minor; pauses during refrains, returns to original G afterward and in the ending.
layers: Rising/falling themes developed into five-note C-minor call-and-response phrases
minor-slide harmony developed in refrains and ending
C-minor melodic hook and triplet fills lowered two octaves onto a synthesized tuba-like low-brass instrument, underneath the pulse
independent sub-bass progression C / Ab / Eb / G, with 8/3-beat triplet intervals in refrains and 4/3-beat triplets in verses
chime-easter-egg.export: scripts/render-chime-easter-egg.cjs schedules the entire offline composition and suppresses wall-clock completion timers while rendering. Verify 60-second PCM duration, audible signal in every one-second window, finite samples and unclipped peaks. Rising/falling motifs follow 225 BPM with freely arranged rhythms.
chime-easter-egg.ending: No one-minute constraint. Final resolving C-minor chord and oboe tonic at beat 232 sustain for eight beats and taper toward ppp. Preview allows the release/effects to finish; no master fade or hard duration cutoff.
chime-easter-egg.groove: Even unchanged pulse anchors syncopated bass notes and anticipated tuba phrase notes. Longer bass triplets retain their spacing. Quiet pickup kicks and snare ghost notes add off-beat accents; five-note C-minor call-and-response phrases vary rhythm on the 225 BPM grid.

intro.description: G2 x8, Eb2 x8, F2 x8, G3 x8. Bass and snare join together during the fourth group at beat 24. Kick at 32, synth at 40, slides at 48, shawm last at 56. Each stage lasts eight beats, with earlier layers continuing. Main begins at beat 64.

chime-easter-egg.tuba-phrasing: Predominantly long, spacious melodic notes. Only three three-note triplet fills: pickups into the two refrains at beats 62 and 126, and the closing fill at beat 206. The final G2 of that fill holds about 4.3 seconds.
chime-easter-egg.expression: Tuba uses a rounder additive low-brass spectrum, a gentler attack, and per-note noteDelayMs values varying between 7 and 24 ms. Pulse stays on the exact grid. Three strategic triplet fills remain available.

async-operation-lifecycle.status: Approved shared command ownership integrated locally; automated tests pass. Deployment and physical microphone verification pending.
async-operation-lifecycle.owner: Every speech chain and pointer state-changing action owns a command operation. Nested actions share the parent. Every recognition wait, validation check, persistence attempt and cancellation belongs to an owner.
invariants: No persistence writes before command validation and required recognition results resolve.
Confirmed and reverted are terminal; late callbacks cannot create new writes or actions under settled owners.

Only explicit tracked waits may keep a command pending. Recognition final-result waits expire and reject after a bounded deadline; valid retryable network failures retain optimistic UI under the existing retry policy.
New utterances may capture immediately; requested final results for earlier accepted commands remain routable until completion or explicit cancellation.
Cancellation and rollback settle once, including all dependent actions, after cooperating or late callbacks have finished.
Applying must describe a tracked executing/validating/committing operation, never a discarded callback. Recognition awaiting-result is a separate lifecycle phase.
Login remains non-optimistic and outside the state-changing command pipeline.
async-operation-lifecycle.known_test_baseline: The loopback-only fixture fails on trip mode in both current production source and isolated prototype. This is not evidence that all suites pass.
async-operation-lifecycle.validation_and_retry: Validation work remains tracked in the transaction. Retry status and attempts are exposed separately. Phase-specific UI wording and exhaustive state invariant enforcement are deferred.

state-validity.status: Initial explicit mainline validity rules; not yet exhaustive or runtime-enforced. Existing unresolved transition guards remain unresolved.
state-validity.model: Visible state = focus plus trip attributes plus orthogonal recognition, configuration and operation lifecycle regions. Node identity alone is not a validity check.
global: An active break/lunch/down interval requires an active trip.
Voicepad must not remain open when recognition is off or sleeping; transition automatically to numberpad. Temporary suspension for playback is distinct from disabling recognition.
Confirmation requires a valid current value; an empty editor cannot confirm.
An optimistic active trip may temporarily lack its permanent ID only while an owned validated start operation is pending.
A rejected operation restores its prior valid state and cancels dependent operations.
No pending operation may exist without an owner, outstanding result/work, or an explicit retry condition.
unresolved: Scheduled draft timing/duration validity needs an explicit draft attribute in the global state.
Exact availability and authorization for each transition need executable predicates from the shared state, not prose placeholders.
Clock phase and Auto goal/range combinations require a full cross-region validity audit.
Drop-In connection validity must be checked independently of watched trip state and local viewer overrides.

drop-in-settings.trip_log: Read-only trips of selected observed user, filtered to selected range. Requires active authorized peer and unexpired publisher session. User switching/disconnect invalidates outstanding requests.
drop-in-settings.exit: Close all streams, stop observer timer and audio, return to landing with session retained. Logout also ends authenticated session.
drop-in-settings.layout: Shared timer header: hamburger followed by Mode filling remaining width. Selected user name appears only in user selection. No redundant dash/name header. Timer fits available viewport; message composer sits directly beneath it without document scrolling. Hamburger omits Sync Goals and User Details; Sync control stays beside the goal in the main timer summary. Hamburger menu and promoted submenus stay at least 12 pixels inside the left/right viewport edges and 8 pixels above the trainer message area. Boundary tracking responds to resizing and message-area height changes; excess menu content scrolls internally. Mode button uses a consistent 12-pixel gap between mirror icon, label and source badge.
drop-in-settings.message_feedback: A nonempty incoming trainer.tts message starts observer-message, a dedicated eighties attention alert with the retained final upper-midrange E6/B5 square-wave pair (200 ms onset spacing, longer final note), before its trimmed, capped 500-character speech. Use announcement timing and padding; preserve broadcast:false for private text. Ignore unrelated and empty messages.

message_templates.picker: Typing an unescaped [ inserts the opening bracket and opens the name picker. First/middle/last/preferred choices show selection order; Insert replaces the opening bracket with the ordered combination; Clear resets choices; Cancel or Escape removes the opening bracket. Escaped \[ bypasses the picker and renders as a literal [ on delivery. The existing settings circled question-mark help explains this behavior.

Retain input and failed recipients on partial failure; uncheck successful recipients to avoid retrying them. Clear input only after all selected recipients succeed.
message_templates.names: Server resolves current first/middle/last/preferred names for each recipient in bracket order, falls back from a blank/missing preferred name to first name, omits other missing parts, and preserves unknown placeholders. Optional middle name is persisted on the user account and editable in Edit Profile.

Toggle notifications synchronize hidden and aria-expanded from current native state; stale close events cannot hide a reopened menu. Shared Mode menus use the same state reader.
